newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG denied rehearing on rate suspension.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG denied rehearing on rate suspension.

text.p: The New York Public Service Commission Thursday denied New York State Electric & Gas Corp's request for a rehearing of the commission's order suspending the second stage of an electric rate increase approved in 1995, commission spokesman David Flanigan said.
The commission "felt that the issues raised (by the rate increase) should be considered in light of the plan the utility filed in the competitive opportunities case," he said.
Flanigan also said the deadline for negotiations on the competitive opportunities filings has been extended until February 14 from January 17.

Besides NYSEG, late September or October 1 filings in the case were made by Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc, Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp and Rochester Gas & Electric Corp.
In its filing, NYSEG proposed a rate freeze for five years following implementation of the rate increases the commission approved for the utility in 1995.
At that time, New York regulators approved rate increases of 2.9 percent, 2.8 percent and 2.7 percent, effective August 1 1995, 1996 and 1997, respectively.

In August, however, the commission declined to approve NYSEG's rate design for years two and three of the agreement which were presented to the regulators three months earlier. In that ruling, the commission put the rate increases on hold until December 30, 1996. Now it has made them part of the competitive opportunity case.
